extracted.intended_audience: journalists, future journalists, and teachers of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Poynter Institute's teaching style, mission, program features, and explicit learning outcomes for seminars and training programs aimed at journalists and journalism educators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small seminar size / individual attention
rubrics_metrics.description: We keep seminars small, which means you get lots of individual attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small class size is emphasized so participants receive personalized instruction and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on instructional approach
rubrics_metrics.description: We emphasize a hands-on approach, so you participate in discussions, case studies, role-playing, and other exercises to get you involved in learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning is active: discussions, case studies, role-playing and practical exercises are core components to involve participants directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality resident and visiting faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Our resident faculty includes distinguished professionals and scholars, all master teachers who bring special expertise to every session. Each seminar also includes visiting faculty, accomplished professionals who leave their jobs for a week to help teach, who spend time with you inside and outside the classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs combine experienced, academically grounded resident faculty with practicing professionals who contribute real-world perspectives and extended interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial independence and mission-focused governance
rubrics_metrics.description: As a financially independent, nonprofit organization, the Institute is beholden to no interest except its own mission: to help journalists do their best work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence from outside interests is presented as a programmatic value that supports editorial and educational integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: excellence and integrity in journalism and leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poynter Institute is a school dedicated to teaching and inspiring journalists and media leaders. It promotes excellence and integrity in the practice of craft and in the practical leadership of successful businesses. It stands for a journalism that informs citizens and enlightens public discourse. It carries forward Nelson Poynter's belief in the value of independent journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mission frames program goals: improving craft, ethical standards, leadership skills, public service journalism, and commitment to independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: courage to take risks and strive for excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: The courage to take risks and to do your best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are expected to gain the confidence to pursue ambitious work and personal excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: increased self-esteem and career agency
rubrics_metrics.description: A higher sense of self-esteem and the power to shape your own career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs aim to strengthen participants' professional identity and ability to direct their career paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: improved confidence in journalistic craft
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training focuses on practical skill-building that leads to measurable gains in craft confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: recognition of the value of diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: A recognition of the value of diversity in the newsroom and in life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity is emphasized as both an ethical value and a practical journalistic asset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: vocabulary to articulate work and values
rubrics_metrics.description: The vocabulary to describe what you do and why, and what you stand for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs provide conceptual language for journalists to explain their roles, choices, and ethical stances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: commitment to ongoing growth and sharing knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: A desire to continue your growth as a journalist and to share what you've learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on lifelong learning and mentorship/knowledge-sharing as part of professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: expanded professional network
rubrics_metrics.description: A new network of people who support you in your work, so your learning continues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Networking and peer support are explicit program goals to sustain post-seminar development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: understanding journalism's role in democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear picture of the special role of journalism in a democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs aim to deepen participants' civic understanding of journalism's public-service responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcome: appreciation of the value and impact of journalistic work
rubrics_metrics.description: An understanding that your life's work is valuable and that you can make a difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training seeks to reinforce meaning and purpose in journalistic careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of learning environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Seminar participants enjoy the variety of learning environments at the Institute: the intense discussion in the seminar rooms, the social interaction in the Great Hall, and the one-to-one conversation in the many small 'break-out' areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program design intentionally provides multiple settings (seminar rooms, social halls, breakout spaces) to facilitate different modes of learning and interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poynter Experience teaching style
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute prides itself on a style of teaching and learning that helps shape every course and seminar we offer into a Poynter Experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Poynter Experience' bundles small size, hands-on methods, expert faculty, and varied learning spaces into a distinctive educational model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional legacy supporting editorial independence and education
rubrics_metrics.description: Nelson Poynter willed the controlling stock of the Times Publishing Company to the Institute to assure its continued independence after his death, and to commit the publishing company's dividends to elevate the standards of journalism through training and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and financial arrangements are presented as guarantees of the Institute's enduring commitment to independence and to funding education/research.
